takeaway: Class II shock: 15-30% blood loss, heart rate above 100, normal blood pressure, urine output 20-30 mL/h, mildly anxious.

question.text: A stabbed 30-year-old is anxious, with a raised respiratory rate, BP 120/105, heart rate 105 and urine 20 mL in the last hour. Which class of shock?
question.say: A stabbed thirty-year-old is anxious, with a raised respiratory rate, blood pressure one twenty over one oh five, heart rate one oh five, and urine twenty mil in the last hour. Which class of shock?

lines.text: This stabbed office worker is anxious but awake. Let us place him on the shock scale.
His blood loss is probably fifteen to thirty percent, and it can hide inside the abdomen.
His heart races at about one hundred and five beats, which is above one hundred.
His urine output is about twenty millilitres an hour, which is reduced.
Yet his blood pressure is still normal. Class two keeps the systolic pressure up.
Mild anxiety, a fast pulse, a faster breathing rate and low urine all fit the second step of the podium.
So the answer is class two shock. Class three would show a falling blood pressure.
